chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the buying of fruit, he said: When it is unspoilt, so there is no problem with buying it.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for buying fruit to be permissible according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'sawa' (equality or uniformity) in fruit sales, indicating that if the fruit is sound and free from hidden defects, the transaction is valid. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on transparency and the absence of 'gharar' (uncertainty) in agricultural commerce, ensuring buyers are not deceived by concealed flaws. This ruling supports the broader Islamic legal principle that sales must be based on clear, ascertainable quality to maintain fairness in market exchanges.
